extractions.value: The diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome was based on the patient’s history, neurological examination, and electrophysiological findings. Diagnosis of this rare condition depends on the clinical findings of axial and proximal limb rigidity, painful spasms, and normal neurological findings, except for brisk deep-tendon reflexes. For definitive diagnosis, it is important to show continuous muscle activity in the trunk and proximal limb muscles at rest. We performed electromyography, showing simultaneous motor-unit firing of the lumbar paraspinal and rectus abdominis muscles at rest.
